title: Scribe ID overhaul: merge learnings, type-aware archive, <TYPE>-<YEAR>-<seq> IDs
problem: Scribe currently maintains two parallel stores (notes and learnings) with duplicated CRUD code and a single global integer counter shared by all note types. Bare numeric IDs in handoffs, commits, and chat do not tell you the type, the global counter grows unbounded forever, and the duplication between notes and learnings is pure maintenance cost. The fix: (1) merge learnings into notes as a `learning` type, (2) make auto-archive type-aware so learnings are exempt, (3) replace the global integer counter with per-(type, year) counters, and (4) render every ID as <TYPE>-<YEAR>-<seq> (e.g. T-2026-1 for todo, H-2025-34 for handoff, L-2026-7 for learning). Each (type, year) bucket starts at seq 1, so growth is bounded — at most one year's worth of one type lives in any single counter.
description:
## Summary of changes

1. Add `learning` to scribe.notes.VALID_TYPES and scribe.store.TYPE_FOLDERS (folder name `learnings`, which already exists from v2). Delete add_learning/get_learning/list_learnings/unlearn_learning from scribe/store.py. Update all callers (notes.py:cmd_learn, cmd_learnings, cmd_unlearn, the learning branch in cmd_get, core/startup.py learning count) to use the unified note paths with note_type='learning'. The scribe/notes.py public surface keeps `learn` as a thin alias for `add --type learning` so muscle memory keeps working.

2. Type-aware auto-archive. Add NEVER_ARCHIVE = {'learning'} as a module-level constant in scribe/notes.py. Update _run_auto_archive_store to skip types in that set. The handoff 'keep only latest per (role, mission)' rule stays exactly as it is and applies across years (so a 2025 handoff gets archived when a 2026 handoff for the same (role, mission) is created).

## Per-(type, year) counters and ID format

3. Drop the global integer counter. The new identifier is a 3-tuple (type, year, seq), rendered as a string display_id like 'T-2026-1' or 'H-2025-34'. Type prefixes: T=todo, H=handoff, D=decision, W=wishlist, R=reference, B=blocker, C=context, G=general, L=learning.

4. New file layout. Each type folder gains per-year subfolders:
```
.apiary/scribe/
  handoffs/
    2025/
      index.jsonl
      next_seq
      1.md, 2.md, ...
    2026/
      index.jsonl
      next_seq
      1.md, 2.md, ...
    archive/
      2025/
        index.jsonl
        ...
  todos/
    2025/...
    2026/...
  learnings/
    2025/...
    2026/...
  ...
```
Body files inside a year folder are named `<seq>.md`. Counter file `<state-dir>/<type>/<year>/next_seq` holds the next seq for that (type, year), each with its own FileLock. Year-rotation/purging is just `rm -rf <type>/archive/<year>/`.

5. Index entry shape. Drop the integer `id` field. Each entry now has:
```
{
  'display_id': 'H-2026-1',
  'type': 'handoff',
  'year': 2026,
  'seq': 1,
  'status': 'active',
  'session': '...',
  'timestamp': '2026-04-12T...',
  'summary': '...',
  'has_body': true,
  'role': 'user',
  'mission': 'general'
}
```
Tests and code paths that read `entry['id']` must switch to `entry['display_id']` (or a tuple of (type, year, seq)).

6. Year detection on write. New notes always take `year = current year at creation time` (UTC). A session that crosses Jan 1 midnight may create H-2026-50 then H-2027-1; that is acceptable.

## Parsing and rendering

7. Generalize _parse_id_arg in scribe/notes.py to accept <TYPE>-<YEAR>-<seq> for every prefix. Bare int and `L<n>` are still accepted for one release for backwards compat (resolved via migration_id_map.json — see step 9).

8. Add _format_id(entry) helper that returns entry['display_id']. Wire it through cmd_list, cmd_get, cmd_done, cmd_update, cmd_archive, every user-facing error message, and core/startup.py:run_summary (active items list, last-session line, notes.py get pointer).

## Migration script

9. Write scripts/migrate_scribe_to_typed_year_ids.py:
   - For each existing note across active and archive, parse its creation timestamp and bucket it as (type, real_year). The 'year' is the year of the note's actual `timestamp` field (UTC).
   - Within each (type, year) bucket, sort entries by timestamp ascending and assign seq starting at 1. Build new display_id strings.
   - Move each `<type>/<old_id>.md` body to `<type>/<year>/<seq>.md`. Same for archived bodies into `<type>/archive/<year>/<seq>.md`.
   - Rewrite the `<type>/<year>/index.jsonl` files atomically (.tmp + replace) using the new entry shape. Drop the old `<type>/index.jsonl` and `<type>/archive/index.jsonl` files.
   - Initialize each `<type>/<year>/next_seq` to (max seq used in that bucket) + 1.
   - Write `<state-dir>/migration_id_map.json` mapping every old identifier to its new display_id. Two key spaces: bare int (`'326': 'H-2026-12'`) and L-prefix legacy (`'L15': 'L-2025-3'`). This file lives at the scribe state root and is loaded lazily by _parse_id_arg for one-release compat.
   - Reference rewriting (programmatic, not audit). Scan and rewrite old-format references in:
     - active handoff bodies (after they have been moved into `handoffs/<year>/<seq>.md`)
     - active learning bodies
     - `<repo-root>/.apiary/scribe/memory/*.md`
     - `<repo-root>/core/commands/*.md`
     - `<repo-root>/scribe/CLAUDE.md`
     Patterns to find and replace: `#<digits>`, `#L<digits>`, `notes.py get <digits>`, `notes.py get L<digits>`. Use the migration map for the lookup. Replace inside fenced code blocks too, since command examples are common. Print a summary of files modified.
   - Backups: before any mutation, copy the entire scribe state dir and the affected docs/memory paths to `<state-dir>/backups/migrate_typed_year_ids/<isodate>/` so a botched run is recoverable. Mirror the pattern in scripts/repair_scribe.py.
   - Out of scope for the rewrite: git history, commit messages, archived note bodies (audit-only — print a list of archived files containing old refs but do not touch them).
   - Support --dry-run (no mutations, prints planned changes) and --force (skip the confirmation prompt) following the conventions in scripts/migrate_scribe_state.py.

## Backwards compat

10. _parse_id_arg accepts three forms during the compat window:
    - `T-2026-1`, `H-2025-34`, etc. (new canonical form)
    - bare integer like `326` (legacy global id) — looked up via migration_id_map.json
    - `L15` (legacy learning) — looked up via migration_id_map.json
    After one release the map and the compat branches are deleted; legacy refs fail with a clear error including the migration map location for manual resolution.

## Tests

11. Extend scribe/test_notes.py with cases for:
    - learning round-trip via the unified note path (add_note note_type='learning', list, get, archive exemption)
    - auto-archive skips learning (NEVER_ARCHIVE)
    - per-(type, year) counter increments independently for different types and years
    - year rollover (mock datetime.now(timezone.utc) to span Jan 1)
    - _parse_id_arg accepts every prefix's canonical form
    - _parse_id_arg accepts bare int + L<n> via the compat map
    - _format_id renders display_id correctly
    - cmd_get / cmd_list / cmd_done / cmd_update use display_id in every output
    - list_notes correctly aggregates across multiple year subfolders

12. New scripts/test_migrate_scribe_to_typed_year_ids.py:
    - renumbering correctness (real_year buckets, timestamp-sorted seq)
    - body file rename for active and archive
    - migration_id_map.json contents (both bare int and L<n> spaces)
    - reference rewriting in synthetic handoff body, learning body, memory file, and a synthetic core/commands/*.md
    - dry-run produces no mutations
    - re-running migration on already-migrated state is a no-op or errors clearly with a 'looks already migrated' message
    - backup directory contains the pre-mutation snapshot

## Doc updates

13. Updates to:
    - scribe/CLAUDE.md (notes table includes learning; document the <TYPE>-<YEAR>-<seq> format with examples; explain per-(type, year) counters)
    - core/commands/wrapup.md (handoff command examples use the new ID format)
    - core/commands/backfill-handoffs.md (agent template uses new IDs)
    - scribe/commands/notes.md (add `learning` to the type list; the `<N>` parsing rule must accept <TYPE>-<YEAR>-<seq> as well as bare int)
    - core/commands/apiary-context.md (any examples that cite a numeric id)
    - docs/reference/cli-tools.md
scope: Modified: scribe/store.py, scribe/notes.py, core/startup.py, scribe/test_notes.py, scribe/CLAUDE.md, core/commands/wrapup.md, core/commands/backfill-handoffs.md, core/commands/apiary-context.md, scribe/commands/notes.md, docs/reference/cli-tools.md. New: scripts/migrate_scribe_to_typed_year_ids.py, scripts/test_migrate_scribe_to_typed_year_ids.py. Out of scope: rewriting git history, editing old commit messages, mutating any reference inside an already-archived note body (the migration only audits and prints a list).
context: Scribe v2 (folder-per-type with <type>/index.jsonl + <id>.md sidecar bodies) is fully in place. Each type folder under .apiary/scribe/ already exists: todos/, handoffs/, decisions/, wishlists/, blockers/, context/, general/, learnings/. Learnings already use the v2 layout but are reached via separate add_learning/get_learning/list_learnings methods in scribe/store.py and the L prefix is hardcoded in _parse_id_arg. Current global counter lives at <state-dir>/next_id. The handoff 'keep only latest per (role, mission)' auto-archive rule lives in _run_auto_archive_store and must NOT be changed by this work. Test suite is 436 tests passing as of commit 46636d9. Portability: stdlib only, UTF-8 everywhere, pathlib for all paths, core/utils/filelock.py:FileLock for concurrent writes. Read scribe/CLAUDE.md and PORTABILITY.md before touching code. Migration script style precedent: scripts/migrate_scribe_state.py and scripts/repair_scribe.py — mirror their --dry-run/--force pattern, their backup-before-mutate convention, and their idempotence checks. The core/utils/filelock.py FileLock is the only acceptable concurrency primitive.
